table.html:

understanding.purpose: Show the clinic schedule by time, day and room, including shared closures and activities that span time slots.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down the time column, then across the Monday and Tuesday room columns to locate or compare activities. Merged cells show when an activity covers multiple times or rooms.
groups: Monday Room A and Room B belong under the Monday header; Tuesday Room A and Room B belong under Tuesday.
All four room columns play the same scheduling role and should remain easy to compare.
The time column identifies each row and can be narrower than the activity columns.
keep_intact: Names, abbreviations and individual words where the available width permits
may_wrap: Long clinic descriptions at word boundaries
The staff training closure across its merged cell
Activities spanning two time slots can use the combined row height for wrapped text

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Keep r1A's three-line cardiology width and reclaim 6px from Monday Room B for Tuesday Room B. Monday Room B still has 97px of text width, matching its longest unbreakable content.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Restore the time label and refine r0B by giving both long activity columns more room while keeping enough width for the shorter entries.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give Tuesday Room B enough width to seek the three-line nutrition wrap seen in r0C, while retaining more room for cardiology and the Monday closure.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Test a wider Monday Room A to improve the cardiology entry, with the remaining width allocated to Tuesday Room B and the short middle columns.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give Tuesday Room B slightly more width than in r1B while restoring 5px to Monday Room A. This tests whether cardiology can wrap more naturally while retaining the shorter nutrition row.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Split the reclaimed space between the two long-description columns. This tests the wrap thresholds between r1A and r1B while preserving enough width for the other room columns.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Move 5px from Tuesday Room B to Monday Room A. Test whether the added width improves the doctor's name or cardiology line breaks while preserving the compact two-slot rows.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give Monday Room A another 5px to explore a more favorable cardiology wrap. Check whether the narrower Tuesday Room B still keeps the nutrition entry readable without adding a line.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The long Monday clinic entry would be squeezed into a narrow column, while shorter entries receive excess space. The resulting extra wrapping would enlarge both time rows and weaken their scan rhythm.
bad.why: The long Monday clinic entry would be squeezed into a narrow column, while shorter entries receive excess space. The resulting extra wrapping would enlarge both time rows and weaken their scan rhythm.

rationale: r2A gives the two long room entries enough width to fit in three lines each, while keeping the time labels and shorter clinic names intact. The two morning rows have matching heights, and the merged cells and day groups remain easy to follow. Its last row is spacious enough for the Tuesday entry without making it disproportionately tall.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading role; columns with long entries may need more space than parallel columns with short entries.
Preserve intact words and identifiers, and judge wrapping by its effect on row rhythm and scanning.
specific: The two long entries compete for width in Monday Room A and Tuesday Room B; r2A gives both a useful three-line wrap.
The time column and the two shorter-content room columns are already close to their practical minimum widths.

tradeoffs: r3A gives Monday Room A a little more room and remains balanced, but its Tuesday entry wraps less naturally, leaving 'type 2 diabetes' on the last line. The taller alternatives remain publishable, though their extra line increases the height of the affected row or rows.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate, based on the supplied renders rather than tests at every pixel. They describe a joint exchange of space between columns 2 and 5, with the other columns held fixed; individual endpoints should not be combined independently. A designer could reasonably prefer r3A's line breaks or accept a taller table for a different balance of column widths.

critique.good: The time labels stay intact, the room columns have a steady rhythm, and the shared closure reads clearly across Monday. The two long activities wrap without breaking words.
critique.problems: The cardiology entry takes four lines, and the nutrition entry makes the final row tall. Short entries leave substantial unused space in the middle columns.
critique.cause: The near-equal 153px room widths give more space than the short entries need while constraining both long descriptions.

critique.good: The wider Monday Room A column reduces the cardiology entry to three lines, and the narrower middle columns still accommodate their short activities. The closure remains on one line.
critique.problems: The 09:00 label splits across lines, disrupting the time column and making the first time slot harder to scan. The nutrition entry still occupies four lines and determines the height of the last row.
critique.cause: The 69px time column leaves one pixel too little for the 49px label after padding and borders. Tuesday Room B at 173px remains too narrow to shorten the nutrition entry substantially.

critique.good: The wide Tuesday Room B column reduces the nutrition entry to three lines, and the shorter room entries remain intact.
critique.problems: The 09:00 label splits, cardiology becomes a narrow five-line block, and the shared closure wraps. The uneven room widths also make the Monday group feel cramped next to Tuesday.
critique.cause: The 69px time column is too narrow for 09:00. Monday Room A at 134px and the combined 258px across Monday give up too much width to Tuesday, especially to the 159px Room A column.

critique.good: The headers and time labels stay intact, and the 09:00 and 10:00 rows have a comfortable, even rhythm. The cardiology description fits in three lines across its two time slots.
critique.problems: The final row is much taller than either time slot above it. The nutrition description occupies four lines, leaving a large area of empty space across the rest of that row.
critique.cause: Monday Room A at 180px gives cardiology enough room for three lines, but Tuesday Room B at 177px leaves only 156px for the nutrition text.

critique.good: The wider Tuesday Room B lets the nutrition description fit in three lines, making the final row shorter. Headers, time labels and individual words remain intact.
critique.problems: The cardiology description now takes four lines, with 10:30 isolated on the last line. Its merged cell makes both earlier time rows taller, so the reduction in the final row does not reduce the overall table height.
critique.cause: Moving 15px from Monday Room A to Tuesday Room B narrows Monday Room A to 165px, below the width needed for the earlier three-line cardiology wrap.

critique.good: The cardiology description fits in three lines, and the headers and time labels remain intact. The two earlier time rows have the same compact height as in r1A.
critique.problems: The extra space in Monday Room A does not improve the visible cardiology wrapping, while the nutrition description still takes four lines and makes the final row disproportionately tall.
critique.cause: Monday Room A at 190px uses 10px more than r1A without reducing its line count; Tuesday Room B consequently drops to 167px.

critique.good: The time labels and room headers stay intact, and the two days are easy to scan. The cardiology entry fits in three lines across its two time slots, keeping those rows relatively compact. The shared closure reads clearly across both Monday rooms.
critique.problems: The cardiology entry breaks the doctor's name across lines. Tuesday Room B has a dense three-line nutrition entry, with a short final line.
critique.cause: Monday Room A is 180px wide, enough for three lines but not enough to keep the name together in this wrapping. Tuesday Room B is 183px wide, so the long nutrition description must wrap.

critique.good: The headers, time labels and individual words stay intact. The wider Tuesday Room B gives the nutrition entry more horizontal space.
critique.problems: The cardiology entry grows to four lines and leaves 10:30 alone on the last line. Its merged cell makes both the 09:00 and 10:00 rows taller, adding space across the other rooms without improving their content. The nutrition entry remains three lines.
critique.cause: Reducing Monday Room A to 170px crosses a wrapping threshold; increasing Tuesday Room B to 193px does not remove a line from its longest entry.

critique.good: The day and room hierarchy remains clear, and text avoids mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Like r2B, the cardiology entry takes four lines, with 10:30 isolated, and makes both associated time rows taller. The extra width in Tuesday Room B does not visibly reduce the nutrition entry's three lines.
critique.cause: Monday Room A at 174px remains below the threshold needed for the three-line wrap seen in r2A; Tuesday Room B at 189px still requires three lines for nutrition.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

contrast.why: The day and room groups are clear, but the narrow Monday Room A column breaks the clinic entry into five lines and makes the morning rows tall.

r2A.why: The room columns are well balanced, and both long entries fit in three lines. The compact rows and clear day groups support comparison.

r1B.why: The groups are clear and the Tuesday entry fits comfortably, though the Monday clinic entry takes four lines and leaves 10:30 alone.

ref_equal.why: The oversized time column takes space from the room columns. Both long clinic entries wrap into five lines, and the training entry also wraps.

ref_auto.why: The two long entries each fit in three lines, with clear day groups and compact, readable rows. The doctor’s name stays together.

r1A.why: The Monday clinic entry fits in three lines, but the narrower Tuesday Room B column makes the nutrition entry four lines and leaves more unused space in the adjacent column.

raw.unsure: B is very close; E keeps the doctor’s name together, while B gives Tuesday Room B slightly more space.

r1A.why: The time column is compact and the schedule is easy to scan, but the long Tuesday entry wraps to four lines and leaves a tall final row.

contrast.why: The day groups are clear, but the narrow Monday Room A column breaks the cardiology entry into five lines, making the first two time slots unnecessarily tall.

ref_equal.why: The oversized time column takes space from the clinic entries. Both long entries wrap heavily, and the training notice also breaks across lines.

r1B.why: The columns are well grouped and the training notice stays on one line, though the cardiology entry wraps to four lines and makes the morning rows taller.

r2A.why: The compact time column leaves useful space for the clinic entries. Both long entries fit in three lines, the training notice stays intact, and the day groups scan clearly.

ref_auto.why: The balanced room columns keep both long entries to three lines and preserve a clear, compact schedule. The training notice remains on one line.

raw.unsure: E and F differ only slightly in their column proportions; either is a strong choice.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
